[ The thesis ]

Page-builders are wonderful. For an about page, a pricing table, a blog — drag, drop, ship, done. We mean it. But somewhere between stack of static rectangles and a thing that responds, computes, remembers and surprises, the blocks run out. This site is everything that lives in that gap.

01 / The case, briefly

A block describes content.
The web can run a program.

It computes

A block stores what you typed. A program decides what to draw sixty times a second based on your cursor, the clock, and a little math. There's no "live particle field" block — because the answer is different every frame.

It has state

Score, position, history, audio context, a physics world. Blocks are stateless rectangles; apps remember. The moment your page needs to know "what happened a second ago," you've left the grid.

It talks back

Drag, fling, strum, type, scroll — and the page answers in real time. Not a hover color change. A simulation reacting to you. That conversation is the whole point of the open web.

02 / Exhibit A through F

Six small things a block can't be

All running right now, on this page, in plain JavaScript. Touch them.

Canvas · Physics live

1 · Fling some gravity

A verlet-integrated physics world with collisions and walls. Grab a ball and throw it. It carries momentum because the page is actually simulating, not animating a fixed clip.

Drag-and-fling with a mouse or finger

Web Audio live

2 · A synth made of math

No audio files. Each note is an oscillator generated on the fly with its own envelope. Press the keys, or play your A S D F G H J K row.

Sound starts on first interaction (browser policy)

Generative live

3 · Art with a seed, not a file

Every render is a fresh, deterministic composition from a random seed — seed 0x00000000. There are billions. You'll likely never see this exact one again.

Click the canvas to regenerate

Realtime input live

4 · Type, and watch it react

Every keystroke spawns a burst of particles with gravity. The page is listening to your input event-by-event and rendering the consequence. A text block just… holds text.

Start typing in the field above

Cursor-reactive live

5 · A surface that feels your cursor

A lattice of points springs away from your pointer and snaps back. Custom-cursor / magnetic UI is a whole craft — and it's pure per-frame vector math, not a setting in a panel.

Move your cursor across the field

Math · Dataviz live

6 · Drive a strange attractor

Thousands of points plotting a Clifford attractor, redrawn live. Drag the slider to warp the equation and the whole structure reorganizes. This is interactive data, not a picture of data.

Slide to mutate the equation

03 / scroll choreography

Scroll isn't a page break.
It's a timeline.

The constellation behind these words is reading your scroll position. Keep going — it assembles as you read. This whole section is one canvas reacting to one number: how far down you are.

03 / scroll choreography

Scattered points
find their order.

A block editor can place things in a column. It cannot say "between 30% and 60% of the way down this section, rotate a 3D point cloud and draw the links as they get close." That's a function of scroll, evaluated every frame.

03 / scroll choreography

The story and
the visual are one.

Progressive reveal, parallax, pinned scenes, scrubbed animation — the grammar of modern editorial storytelling. None of it is content you stack. It's behavior you write. The dial in the corner is your progress.

03 / scroll choreography

So… how would
you do this?

You wouldn't, in blocks. And that's fine — blocks were never for this. The point is only that "more" exists, it's open, it runs in every browser, and it's built by hand. Like this page was.

Blocks for the content.
Code for the magic.

Use the right tool for each job — and when the job is an experience that listens, computes, and surprises, remember that the browser has always been able to do far more than fill in rectangles.
